reason: Uriah the Hittite, a regular person (a soldier without royal status), is portrayed with exceptional moral favor. The text emphasizes his integrity and principled character through his refusal to go home when the king commands him, reasoning that he cannot enjoy comfort while the ark and Israel are in the field (11:11). Even when David attempts to manipulate him through drunkenness, Uriah maintains his principles and refuses to return home (11:13). He is presented as righteous, loyal, and of strong moral character—serving as a stark contrast to the king's wickedness. His innocence and victimization further establish him as a sympathetically portrayed regular person.
